parts.label: d
parts.text: When the Group 1 elements react with water, each of their atoms loses an electron from its outer shell. For sodium and potassium, these processes can be represented by the equations $\begin{array}{l} \cdot \mathrm {N a} \rightarrow \mathrm {N a} ^ {+} + \mathrm {e} ^ {-} \\ \cdot \mathrm {K} \rightarrow \mathrm {K} ^ {+} + \mathrm {e} ^ {-} \\ \end{array}$ Explain, by referring to the electronic configurations of sodium and potassium, why potassium is more reactive than sodium.

questions.stem: Most experiments involving electrolysis use inert electrodes, which do not take part in the reactions. However, in some experiments the electrodes do take part in the reactions. She uses this method. weigh two clean strips of copper use one strip as the positive electrode and the other as the negative electrode after electrolysis wash the strips of copper with ethanol (a liquid that boils at $ 7 8^{\circ} \mathrm{C} $) dry the strips of copper and reweigh them The ionic half-equations for the reactions at the electrodes are Positive electrode $\mathrm {C u} (\mathrm {s}) - 2 \mathrm {e} ^ {-} \rightarrow \mathrm {C u} ^ {2 +} (\mathrm {a q})$ Negative electrode $\mathrm {C u} ^ {2 +} (\mathrm {a q}) + 2 \mathrm {e} ^ {-} \rightarrow \mathrm {C u} (\mathrm {s})$ A student investigates the electrolysis of copper(II) sulfate solution using copper electrodes which do take part in the reaction. She uses this apparatus.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Suggest why the copper strips would dry more quickly when washed with ethanol rather than with water.

parts.label: b
parts.text: The student's results are shown in the table. The table shows that the decrease in mass of the positive electrode was 0.32 g.

parts.label: b-i
parts.text: Calculate the increase in mass, in grams, of the negative electrode.

parts.label: b-ii
parts.text: The ionic half-equations show that the increase in mass of the negative electrode should be the same as the decrease in mass of the positive electrode. Suggest two reasons why the increase in mass of the negative electrode in the student's experiment was less than expected.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Another student investigated the effect of changing the electrical charge, in faradays, passed during the electrolysis. parts.label: c-iii
parts.text: Suggest why the straight line should go through the origin.

parts.label: c-iv
parts.text: Explain why the graph shows that the increase in mass is directly proportional to the electrical charge passed.

parts.label: c-v
parts.text: Use your graph to estimate the increase in mass, in grams, of the copper electrode that would be produced by passing an electrical charge of 0.55 faradays.
